title: Queue-shepherding: Continuous-batcher grace-periods and starvation-detector
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We observed recurring tail-latency spikes in continuous-batching under mixed workloads where small, KV-heavy requests were frequently starved by large non-KV batches. Existing fairness heuristics (age-based bump + quantile admission) reduced the symptom but left intermittent starvation and noisy timeouts. This PR implements a "queue-shepherding" scheduler overlay that enforces per-queue grace periods, an opt-in starvation detector, and tighter admission/commit timeouts to stabilize tail latency without sacrificing throughput. Implementation summary: - Add pkg/batcher/queue_shepherd.go: new lightweight coordinator that tracks per-queue 'grace windows' and per-request age; it maintains a small circular buffer of queue head timestamps and computes when a queue is eligible for promotion. - Modify pkg/batcher/scheduler.go to consult the shepherd for admission decisions: queues that exceed grace are prioritized for the next batch slice, within a configurable cap to avoid throughput erosion. - Starvation detector: background goroutine that samples queue age distribution and triggers bounded promotions if a queue's median age exceeds threshold; promotion is rate-limited by a token bucket to avoid thrashing. - KV cache cooperation: pkg/kv/cache_manager.go exposes a new soft-pin hint so shepherd can avoid evicting pinned KV entries when promoting aged KV-heavy requests; added an eviction backoff for pinned entries to reduce spikey evictions. - Timeouts tuning: admissionTimeout reduced from 20ms to 12ms for typical low-latency routes; commitWindow shortened by 10% for busy autoscaling pools to reduce tail amplification. - Observability: internal/observability/metrics.go adds batcher.promotions_total, batcher.grace_period_expires, and batcher.queue_age_seconds_histogram. Docs: docs/runbooks/batcher_tuning.md documents feature-flag, Helm values, and canary steps. Tests: tests/batcher/integration_test.go covers starvation scenarios; added unit tests for promotion bounding and KV soft-pin behavior. Commits: - 1f9c3a2: Introduce queue_shepherd skeleton and interfaces - 2b7d1f4: Hook shepherd into admission path and unit tests - 4c13b88: Add starvation detector + backpressure rate limiter - a9e2b7d: KV soft-pin hint and eviction backoff - 0d3e5aa: Add metrics + docs + helm flag - 7f8b2c1: Fix race on promotion queue and add lock + CI fixes Key configuration (canary defaults): - batcher.queue_shepherding.enabled = false (helm values set true for canary clusters) - batcher.queue_shepherding.grace_ms = 30 - batcher.queue_shepherding.promotion_rate = 50 reqs/s - batcher.admission.timeout_ms = 12 Performance (canary, KV-heavy mixed workload): - Baseline (no shepherd): token 95th = 210ms, p50 = 18ms, throughput = 1.00x - With shepherd enabled (canary): token 95th = 151ms (-28%), p50 = 19ms (+1ms noise), throughput = 0.99x (-1%) - Under extreme KV-pinned workload: 95th improved from 360ms to 235ms (-35%) without increasing request failures. Safety & rollout: - Feature gated behind helm flag and runtime feature flag. - Canary rollout: enable in 5% capacity for 24h; monitor batcher.promotions_total, queue_age histogram, token error rate, and KV eviction spikes. - If promotions_total spikes > 5x baseline or eviction spikes appear, rollback immediately. Review summary and conversation: "Marco Alvarez" raised a race in promoteAgedRequests vs eviction which could allow double-promotion; added a promotion mutex and promotion counter metric as requested. "Chen Li" requested a feature flag and a Helm value — added both and updated docs with canary steps. "Aisha Patel" asked for more representative KV-heavy numbers and tighter assertions in integration tests — added microbench harness and increased test determinism. CI history: initial run failed two flaky tests (data race in scheduling_test) — fixed by adding a promotion lock and reworked test harness; subsequent runs pass. Merge: changes approved by Marco and Chen after two iterative fixes; Aisha gave final sign-off post-canary validation. Rollout plan executed and shepherd was enabled in canary clusters for 72 hours; observed stable promotions and no eviction regressions; merged to main.

release_notes: Introduce queue-shepherding (opt-in) to improve fairness and prevent starvation in continuous-batching. New metrics and a feature flag for canary. Typical 95th token latency reductions of ~28-35% on KV-heavy small-batch workloads without noticeable throughput loss.
